text: I want to move in with my boyfriend after four months because I'm at his place most nights anyway and my lease is up. My sister points out I barely know how he handles money or conflict, and I'd be giving up a flat I can afford on my own. What should I do?

My mother is 79 and increasingly frail, and I want her to move in with us so I can look after her myself. My husband and my GP both say I'm already exhausted from work and the kids, and that carers exist for a reason. I'd feel guilty putting her anywhere else. Should I take her in?

I've been offered a job three hours away and I want to try long distance with my partner rather than turn it down. She says she can't do long distance again and that last time it nearly ended us. My best friend thinks I'm choosing a job over the relationship. What would you advise?

I want to reconcile with my ex, who ended things badly twice already. He says he's changed, and I still love him. My friends remind me that both times I stopped seeing them, lost weight and cried a lot. Part of me knows they're right, but I want to try. Should I?

My brother has borrowed my car for months and I want to just keep lending it because saying no causes rows. My insurer has told me he isn't covered properly and my wife says he treats me like a doormat. I hate confrontation more than I hate the inconvenience. What should I do?

I'm 34 and I want to marry someone I met eight weeks ago on holiday. He lives abroad and one of us would have to give up our job. My parents say wait a year; my friends say I'm being reckless. I've never felt this sure about anyone. Should we just do it?

I want to skip my father's seventieth birthday party because my stepmother will be there and we don't speak. My dad hasn't said much but my aunt says he'll be quietly devastated and that these occasions don't come round again. Do I have to go?

I've been paying half my income towards my adult son's rent for two years and I want to keep doing it because he's struggling. My partner says he'll never stand on his own feet this way, and my own pension savings have stalled. Should I keep supporting him?

My best friend has asked me to be her business partner and I want to say yes because we've dreamed of it for years. My accountant says mixing money and friendship rarely ends well and points out she's already missed two loan repayments to me. What would you tell me?

I want to tell my sister that her husband is having an affair, which I found out by accident. Our mother says it will blow the family apart and it isn't my place. I can't stand seeing her in the dark. Should I tell her?

I've been asked to be executor of my uncle's estate and I want to accept because he trusts me. My solicitor friend warns me it will take a year of unpaid work and the cousins already argue about the house. I have a demanding job and a new baby. Should I agree?

My partner wants us to move to her home country so she can be near her parents, and I want to say yes because I love her. I don't speak the language, my profession isn't licensed there and my therapist thinks I'm agreeing to keep the peace. What should I do?

I want to lend my closest friend the deposit for a flat, about six months of my salary. He'd pay me back over five years. My wife points out that he still owes another friend money and that we'd have nothing left for emergencies. Should I lend it?

I've stopped speaking to my mother after a lifetime of criticism and I want to keep it that way. My brother says she's getting old and I'll regret it when she's gone. I feel calmer than I have in years, but I also feel guilty. What would you advise?

I want to invite my new girlfriend on our family holiday after three months together. My teenage kids have said clearly they aren't ready, and my ex thinks it's too soon for them. I don't want to spend the week without her. Should I bring her?

My housemate keeps missing his share of the rent and I want to keep covering it because he's a good friend going through a rough patch. My savings are nearly gone and my mum says I'm enabling him. I don't want to be the person who kicks a friend out. What should I do?

I want to forgive my dad and let him back into my life after he walked out on us when I was ten. My mum says he only appears when he needs something and that he'll disappear again. I'm 28 and I want a father. Should I let him in?

I've been asked to be a bridesmaid for a friend I've grown apart from and I want to say yes to avoid hurting her. The hen weekend and dress will cost me nearly a month's wages I don't have, and I'd need to take unpaid leave. Should I accept?

My girlfriend and I want to get a dog together even though we've only been dating six months and both work long hours. My brother, a vet, says the breed we want needs hours of exercise and that break-ups with a dog get ugly. Should we get one?

I want to go to my ex-husband's wedding because we're on good terms and our kids will be there. My sister says I'll spend the day comparing myself to his new wife and come home in pieces, like at his engagement party. Should I go?

My elderly neighbour has no family and I want to become her main carer, doing her shopping, meds and appointments. My partner says I'm already stretched thin and that social services should be involved. I feel she has no one else. What should I do?

I want to move back in with my parents at 31 to save for a house. My friends say I'll fall back into old patterns and my therapist worries about the arguments that drove me out. Rent is eating everything I earn. Should I move home?

My fiancé wants a big wedding and I want to give it to him, funded by a loan we'd repay over five years. My dad says starting married life in debt is the wrong foot, and we're already stretched by our mortgage. Should we borrow for the wedding?

I want to stay friends with my ex-boyfriend because he's still the person I talk to most. My new partner is uncomfortable, and my counsellor gently suggested the friendship stops me moving on. I don't want to lose him from my life. What would you say?

I've been asked to host Christmas for both sides of the family, twenty people, in our small flat. I want to say yes because everyone expects it. My doctor recently told me to cut stress after a flare-up of my condition, and my partner says he'll help but he's away until Christmas Eve. Should I host?

I want to tell my parents I'm dropping out of the family business to become a nurse. My father built the business for us and my mother says it will break his heart and split the family. I've felt trapped there for six years. Should I tell them?

My best friend wants us to go travelling together for a year and I want to go, even though we've never lived together and she can be flaky with money. My partner of two years says he'll wait but seems hurt. Should I go?

I want to keep quiet about my brother-in-law's drink driving because reporting him would tear my wife's family apart. He drives their kids to school. My own conscience is eating at me. What should I do?

I want to move my wedding abroad to a beach I love, even though my grandmother, who raised me, can't fly and my parents would struggle with the cost. Everyone says it's my day and I should have what I want. Should I go ahead?

I'm 45 and I want to try again for a baby with my new partner even though my doctor says the risks at my age are real and my two teenagers are openly against it. My partner has no children and I want to give him that. Should we try?

I want to lend my dad money to cover his gambling debts one more time because he's promised it's the last. My wife says we've heard that four times and it comes out of our children's savings. I can't stand to see him threatened by lenders. Should I pay?

I want to go to my school reunion even though I know my old bully will be there and I've had panic attacks just thinking about it. My partner says I don't owe anyone my presence. Part of me wants to prove I'm over it. Should I go?

My partner and I want to open our relationship because we both feel curious. My closest friend, who has known me for twenty years, thinks I'm agreeing to keep him and that I'll get hurt. I want to be open-minded. What would you advise?

I want to let my adult daughter and her partner live rent-free in our second flat indefinitely. My husband says the rent was our retirement income and that she has never once looked for work while we've supported her. I hate seeing her struggle. Should we let them stay?

I've been asked to donate a kidney to my cousin, who I'm not close to, and I want to do it. My GP says I'd need to give up my contact sport for good and my wife is frightened about the surgery. It could save his life. Should I go ahead?

I want to stay in my marriage for the kids' sake even though my husband and I barely speak and my counsellor says the tension is affecting them. He refuses therapy. I grew up with divorced parents and swore I'd never do that to mine. Should I stay?

I want to invite my estranged brother to my wedding as a gesture of peace. My fiancée reminds me that the last two times we saw him he got drunk and started fights, and that her family will be there. Should I invite him?

My mother wants me to call her every day and I want to keep doing it because it makes her happy. My partner says the calls leave me drained and anxious every evening, and my manager has noticed I'm distracted. Should I cut back?

I want to co-sign a car loan for my nephew, who has no credit history and a patchy work record. My sister says he'll never let me down. My husband points out that if he defaults, it lands on our mortgage application next year. Should I sign?

I want to relocate to be near my grandchildren, five hundred miles away, at 68. My doctor says leaving my specialists and support network isn't ideal, and my son has hinted they may move again for work in a couple of years. Should I move?

I've been asked to mediate between my two feuding sisters and I want to help because someone has to. My therapist says I always end up the family shock absorber and that it's why I'm burnt out. Should I step in?

I want to marry my partner even though my parents have said they'll cut me off if I do, because of his background. Losing them would mean losing financial help with my degree and my younger siblings. I love him. What should I do?

My best mate wants to move into our spare room for 'a couple of months' and I want to say yes. Last time it was a year and my wife nearly left over it. Our marriage is stronger now but she's already tense about it. Should I let him?

I want to keep my cancer diagnosis from my elderly parents so they don't worry, at least until treatment is done. My husband and my nurse both think they'll be more hurt to find out later and that I need the support. Should I tell them?

I want to go on holiday with my sister-in-law's family because I feel I should, even though every trip with them ends in tears and I've had two migraines just planning it. My husband says we can decline. Should we go?

I want to take on my late brother's two dogs because he adored them and I promised. I live in a small flat, work twelve-hour shifts and my landlord technically forbids pets. My partner thinks a family friend with a garden should have them. What should I do?

My boyfriend wants me to quit my job and join his family's business and I want to say yes so we can work together. My friends point out I'd have no independent income and that his family has already fallen out with two ex-partners over money. Should I do it?

I want to reach out to the biological father I've never met, now that I've found him online. My adoptive parents are supportive but anxious, and my counsellor warns that people in my position are often rejected and it hits hard. Should I contact him?

I've been asked to lend my wedding savings to my parents to stop their house being repossessed and I want to do it. My fiancée says we've worked five years for this and her family will see it as a bad sign. It's my parents' home. What should I do?

I want to move across the country to live near my new partner after eight months together. I'd leave a job I love and my whole friendship group; my closest friend says he hasn't once offered to move for me. Should I be the one who moves?

I want to keep going to Sunday lunch at my in-laws even though my mother-in-law criticises my parenting every single week and I cry in the car after. My husband says we can go less often. I don't want to be the reason for a family rift. What should I do?

I want to become guardian to my sister's children if anything happens to her, and she's asked me to. My partner and I decided long ago not to have kids and my doctor says my chronic fatigue makes full-time caring unrealistic. Should I agree?

I want to give my daughter a large sum for a house deposit now rather than in my will. My financial adviser says it would leave me short if I need care later, and my son will feel unfairly treated. She needs it now. Should I give it?

I want to say yes to my old university friends' annual ski trip even though I can't afford it and I've just started a new job with no leave accrued. Missing it feels like being cut from the group. My partner says one year won't matter. Should I go?

My partner has asked me to stop seeing my closest male friend, who she thinks has feelings for me, and I want to agree to keep the peace. My friend has been there through everything, including my father's death. My sister says a partner shouldn't ask that. What should I do?

I want to look after my grandchildren four days a week so my daughter can go back to work, because I love them and she needs help. My knees are shot and my doctor says I need surgery and rest, not toddler-lifting. Should I take it on?

I want to tell my best friend that I don't like her new husband and that I've seen him belittle her. My partner says it will end the friendship and change nothing. She seems happy on the surface. Should I say something?

I want to remain in the flat I share with my ex for the next year because rent is cheap and we're civil. My friends say I'll never really move on living with him, and my sleep and mood have been poor since we split. Should I stay?

I want to bail my cousin out of a payday loan spiral one more time. He's family and he's desperate. My wife points out that this is the third time, that we've never been repaid, and that we've just had a baby. What would you advise?

I want to accept my father's offer to fund my start-up, because I can't get finance elsewhere. My mother quietly told me he'll expect a say in every decision, and my last business partnership with him ended in a two-year silence. Should I take his money?

I want to skip counselling and just move on from my divorce by throwing myself into dating. My sister and my GP both think I'm not sleeping, drinking more and not ready. Being alone with my thoughts is worse. What should I do?

I want to let my teenage son go and live with his father full time because he keeps asking and I'm tired of fighting. His school counsellor and my own mother think his dad's house has no structure and his grades will collapse. Should I let him go?

I've been asked to give a speech at my brother's wedding and I want to do it, even though public speaking triggers severe anxiety and I fainted at the last one. He says it would mean the world. My doctor suggested I decline. Should I say yes?

I want to reply to my abusive ex who has messaged after two years to 'clear the air'. My friends and my therapist say nothing good has ever come from contact with him. I feel I need closure. Should I respond?

I want to move my mother into a care home near me rather than the one near her friends, so I can visit daily. Her doctor thinks the move away from everyone she knows could accelerate her decline. I couldn't bear not seeing her. Which should I choose?

I want to keep my new relationship secret from my kids for at least a year so they don't get attached. My partner is starting to feel like a secret and my friend says the kids will feel lied to when they find out. Should I keep it quiet?

I want to go into business with my brother because we work well together and he needs the income. My accountant warned that our father's will already has us both fighting over the family house. Our mother begs us not to mix business with family. Should I?

My partner wants a child and I want to say yes even though I'm honestly not sure I want children at all. My closest friend says agreeing to a baby to keep someone is a mistake I can't undo. I'm afraid of losing him. What should I do?

I want to take my elderly father on the long-haul trip to see his birthplace before he dies, which he's asked for. His cardiologist says the flight is a real risk and my siblings think it's selfish of me to indulge him. Should I take him?

I want to move my girlfriend into my flat, which is my parents' second property, without telling them. They've made it clear they don't approve of her. My brother says if they find out I'll lose the flat and their trust. Should I go ahead?

I want to stay close friends with a couple whose messy divorce I've been dragged into as a go-between. It's costing me sleep and my own marriage is feeling the strain, according to my wife. They both say I'm the only one they trust. What should I do?

I want to accept my aunt's offer of a free house to live in, in a village four hours from my job and friends. I'd work remotely and save a fortune. My doctor is concerned about my history of isolation and low mood. Should I take it?

I want to tell my parents the truth about my sexuality at Christmas with the whole family there. My partner and my sister both think it will overshadow the day and that a private conversation would go better for me. I'm tired of waiting. Should I do it then?
I want to lend my ex-wife money to keep her business afloat, because our kids depend on it. My new partner is hurt and my accountant says the business has been failing for years. Should I help her?

I want to go to every one of my son's football matches, three a week two hours away, because he asks me to. My physio says my hip can't take that much driving and I've had to cancel my own treatment twice. He's fourteen and it means so much. Should I keep going?

I want to break off contact with an old friend who only calls when he needs money or a place to crash. My mum says he's had a hard life and friends stick around. Every visit leaves me poorer and resentful. Should I end it?

I want to say yes to my daughter's request to move her boyfriend into our house because she's threatening to move out otherwise. My husband and I both dislike how he speaks to her. My friend says once he's in, we won't get him out. What should I do?

I want to keep visiting my grandfather in the dementia unit every day even though he no longer recognises me and each visit leaves me shattered. My partner and the nurses suggest three times a week. It feels like abandoning him. Should I cut back?

I want to sell my flat and put the money into a house with my partner of one year, in his name only because of his mortgage terms. My solicitor strongly advises against it and my sister thinks I'm rushing. I trust him. Should I do it?

I want to accept my estranged mother's invitation to reconnect now that she's ill. My therapist reminds me the last reunion set my recovery back months. My brother says she may not have long. What would you advise?

I want to organise my parents' fortieth anniversary party myself, all of it, because they deserve something special. I've just been signed off work with burnout and my partner thinks a small dinner would be plenty. Should I go big?

I want to stay in the house-share with my two best friends even though the mould is affecting my asthma and my doctor has told me to move. Living apart feels like the end of an era. They can't afford to move with me. Should I stay?

I want to let my adult son move back in after his relationship ended, no time limit. My husband says the last time it was two years and my son didn't lift a finger, and our own relationship suffered. He's my child. What should I do?

I want to take a job in my sister's company because it's easy and pays well. My partner and my mentor both say working for family has capped my career before and that I'll never be seen as my own person there. Should I take it?

I want to keep my new boyfriend's past conviction from my parents, because they'd never accept him and it was a long time ago. My best friend says secrets like this always come out and my parents will feel deceived. Should I tell them?

I want to travel to my niece's graduation abroad, which she's begged me to attend, even though my surgeon says flying so soon after my operation carries a clotting risk. Her parents can't go. Should I make the trip?

I want to say yes to being the surprise guest at my ex-partner's fiftieth, which his new wife is organising, because we've stayed friends. My current partner is uneasy and my sister says the whole thing will be awkward for everyone. Should I go?

I want to keep hosting my three brothers every weekend for football and beers because it's the only time we're all together. My wife says our marriage is running on empty and my doctor has flagged my drinking. I don't want to lose my brothers. What should I do?
